title: Prebid Server appush adapter exemplary banner fixture, adapted with an iframe-wrapped adm

source.name: prebid/prebid-server — adapters/appush/appushtest/exemplary/simple-banner.json (mockBidRequest + mockResponse)
source.notes: Facts (field shapes), not prose, are reused per the clone's own ATTRIBUTION.md; the fixture's comments/prose are not reproduced. NOTICE file absent upstream, which only removes 4(d), not the licence itself.

modifications: device.ip changed from the fixture's public-looking 123.123.123.123 to the RFC 5737 TEST-NET-3 address 203.0.113.10 — no real IP is retained.

Top-level BidRequest/BidResponse id, imp.id, bid.id renamed to this corpus's id convention; cid/crid/dealid left as the fixture's own literal test constants (already non-functional placeholders in the public fixture, not live identifiers).

The fixture's httpCalls/expectedBidResponses wrapper (a Prebid-Server-internal test-runner shape) is not reproduced; only the plain oRTB mockBidRequest and the oRTB body of mockResponse are kept, since this corpus is about the wire-level oRTB pair, not the adapter test harness.
imp.ext.bidder.placementId is kept unchanged — it is exactly the kind of vendor-adapter ext key this corpus wants represented, and it is not a live identifier.

The adm string (an <iframe> pointing at http://example.com/pserver&k=...) is kept byte-for-byte: example.com is the IANA-reserved documentation domain (RFC 2606), and the k= token is the fixture's own static test constant.
provenance.sanitized: Only synthetic identifiers, original fixture creatives, reserved domains and TEST-NET addresses. No live tokens, subscriber IDs or real tracking URLs.
provenance.notes: vendor-adapter-fixture; see modifications for the one required IP substitution.

pairApplicability.note: The fixture's mockBidRequest/mockResponse.body are a real bid-response-to-bid-request pair (impid resolves, id matches after renaming).

bid.adm: <iframe id="adm-banner-16" width="300" height="250" frameborder="0" marginheight="0" marginwidth="0" style="{overflow:hidden}" src="http://example.com/pserver&k=882b2510ed6d6c94fa69c99aa522a708"></iframe>

specNotes: Protocol validity is based on cited fields, not on current Core output. Optional-field warnings do not make this pair invalid.

imp.ext.bidder is an unrecognized vendor ext key by design — Core's dialects-questions plugin (request-only) is expected to ask about it at question level, which never affects rollupStatus/maxLevel; this is correct behaviour being exercised, not a defect.
The adm is a bare <iframe> element (no surrounding document, no visible label) pointing at a second-hop ad-server URL — this is the real observed Prebid-adapter shape, not an invented one.
The sandboxed preview frame's injected CSP is frame-src 'none' with no data:/blob: exception (public/ortbtools.app.js buildProbedSrcdoc) — a nested

Browser assertions are proposed observables; this corpus has not been run in a browser. Assert the refusal ledger (#creativeBlocked) reports exactly one blocked resource for directive frame-src and host example.com — a deliberate, explained refusal, not a silent empty rectangle.
No marker text exists in this adm at all (it is a single self-closing iframe tag) — this case does not assert expect.preview.marker; it proves the blocked-nested-frame contract path instead.
notes: Core observations in the source archive were deliberately excluded from expectations. Protocol metadata may describe a vendor-specific 2.x carrier; it does not claim a normative minor-version inference.

preview.limitation: The creative is a nested <iframe> tag; the preview frame policy sets frame-src 'none', so the child frame is refused and nothing paints (correct per the 012 contract). The refusal ledger reports the blocked frame.
preview.capabilityGap: No way to inspect an iframe-wrapped tag creative beyond its wrapper markup.
